countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 740 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 870 `.webp` are committed and the 18 `supplementary` sets below account for 130 of them (one of those sets declares no frames), leaving 740. This branch's contribution to those two terms is the sixteen `clear-search/` frames - a live-app set it declares below, so the SWEPT term is unmoved; it ran no sweep, so `head`, `capturedAt` and `dirtyWorkingTree` above are carried over from that run and still describe it, but `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are not: this PR re-stamped them from the sweep's carried pair to its own (`1f3f94fc` to `8af0e673` for `src`, `b94c6290` to `4726627d` for `scripts`); both values move with the base - the `scripts` pair moved again when this branch was rebased onto `#138`, which edited `scripts/` - so a reader should compare them against `git rev-parse HEAD:src HEAD:scripts`, which is the equality `check-evidence.mjs` asserts, rather than against the literals here, which `check-evidence.mjs` requires of any head because that pair is the thing that tells a reader whether the committed frames are pictures of the current source. `head` and `srcTree` here therefore name two different trees by design - the sweep's and this branch's - and a reader reconciling the stamps should read them that way rather than as one capture record. Re-derived for THIS head and stated once. Earlier revisions of this field appended a fresh derivation per merge and left the previous ones standing as though they still described the tree, so it accumulated half a dozen figures from superseded heads and, after the 0.19.5 rebase, a subtraction that no longer resolved - the sibling terms were updated and the remainder was not. Those figures are deleted rather than quoted here: a reader scanning this field for a number should not find a wrong one under any framing. A stale derivation is worse here than no derivation, because this field's entire justification is that a reader can re-compute it: one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. The three terms above are the whole arithmetic, they are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l`, and the summed `frames` of the sets below), and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it - which is what makes the sentence checkable rather than merely asserted. This branch carries no version bump of its own: it is rebased rather than merged, so `package.json` on it reads whatever the base it was rebased onto carried, and a release landing on `main` afterwards only moves the number under a branch that never set it. On this head `package.json` is `0.19.7`, and its rebase base carries the same `0.19.7` - the base is deliberately not named, because every rebase moves it and a literal here has already been wrong twice; read `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` for the current one. The value is the base's, so the claim is "no bump against its base" rather than a number tied to any one head or rebase.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 108 entries, counted off the merged literal rather than summed from the two sides' fields (96 on this branch before the rebase and 107 on `main`, each written by a run taken before the other side landed - which is exactly why the merged figure is counted and not added). `main` brought the model-picker surfaces (11 `chat-model-picker--*` states plus the `chat-session-status-strip--model-switch-pending` band); this branch adds the one story it registered, `chat-tool-rows--trace-gap-boundaries`, and 107 + 1 = 108 is the reconciliation. `check-evidence.mjs` counts the list and fails a mismatch (round 4, R3), so this field cannot silently lag its own source.

partialCapture.note: REBASE RE-STAMP onto `98c32e85e` (`main`, 0.19.7 plus #118, #137 and #138). `main` moved twice under this branch during the round, and this stamp follows the second move: `main`'s delta since the head the frames were last taken at is #138 alone, which is packaging - `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, `docs/BUILD.md`, `docs/CODE_SIGNING.md`, `package.json` and four files under `scripts/` (`prune-python-resource.mjs` and its test, `update-robustness.test.mjs`, `verify-macos-artifacts.mjs`) - and NOT ONE byte of `src/`, which is why `srcTree` below is the same hash this manifest carried before the rebase and only `scriptsTree` moved. The pass's own figures are measured rather than asserted: see `unchangedControl` for the control, `recaptureNote` for what moved and why the committed bytes were kept, and `provenanceNote` for what the rebase did and did not move, including why the live-app set's citation is a replay rather than a re-drive. partialCapture.provenanceNote: THE REBASE. `main` moved twice while this branch was in review - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6, which this branch had already been rebased onto) and then to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138) - and what the second move brings into the tree is packaging only (`package.json`, the publish workflow, three docs, four `scripts/` files), with `src/` byte-identical: the `srcTree` below is the hash this manifest already carried, and the re-capture confirms it rather than assuming it. The result is one-sided again: the four Files surfaces, all twelve control frames and 101 of the 108 frames overall came back byte-identical, and the seven that moved are the same two classes the previous pass measured (`recaptureNote`). The live-app set was NOT re-driven this time, and its citation says so: the frames were taken at `8fc94e602`, whose replay in this history is `71cd00ae0` - a range-diff `=` pair, the same patch - and the renderer source is byte-identical across the rebase, so the pixels on disk are that pass's output for the same source. `capturedAtHead` names the replay of the tree they were taken from, not a claim that a later pass re-took them; the previous rebase re-drove it and got all four frames back as the exact committed bytes, which is the reading that makes the citation honest. The one file the rebase had to resolve by hand is again `package.json`: the resolution keeps `main`'s `version` line (0.19.7) and takes the UNION of the two sides' `test:desktop` file lists, so this branch adds its single test file to `main`'s list and moves no version - which is what the repository's version-bump guard checks.
partialCapture.addedNote: `addedAt`/`addedAtHead` above are the ROUND-2 pass's: they record the last pass that added a surface (`canvas-workspace/files-scan-stopped-empty`, twelve frames, at the replay of the head it ran on), so `addedFrames` 12 and `addedSurfaces` name that pass and not the re-capture that re-stamped it. The distinction is R3-1's: the pass that wrote `refreshedFrames: 48` counted the ADDED story's twelve frames in a number a reader reads as `re-captured in place`, so the two figures were conflated. Round 4 (R4-1) found the pair could not be trusted at all - a re-stamp overwrote `addedAt`/`addedAtHead` with its own run while resetting `addedFrames` to 0 and `addedSurfaces` to `[]`, so the fields named a pass that had added nothing and could not be fetched. `partialAddedFields` in `capture-evidence.mjs` now decides the citation (covered by `evidence-manifest.test.mjs`) and `check-evidence.mjs` holds both head citations to the reachability bar it applies to `head`. This rebase's re-capture found the COUNTS half of the same rule still open - it is a zero-add pass, and `main`'s accumulating writer reset them to 0/[] anyway, which is what these two values were corrected from - so the writer now leaves the whole added-pass record alone unless a run actually adds frames. Both rebase passes since are zero-add passes and the writer left that record alone, which is the corrected behaviour: `addedFrames` 12 and `addedSurfaces` still name the round-2 pass, and only the citation above moves, each time to the new rebase's replay of the same commit.

unchangedControl.why: The honesty check for this pass, and the reason a moved frame is legible as one: a surface this rebase does not paint differently was re-captured through the same command, on the same host, in the same session as the nine it does. All twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the encoder and the renderer are deterministic here at this load. The class the moved frames belong to was measured the same way in the previous pass, which ran `audio-viewer` twice: its `neon` frame - which moved in the first run of BOTH passes - came back exactly the committed bytes in that second run. Neither control separates the widget from the encoder for `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, whose difference is the platform PDF plugin not painting at all and which reproduced byte-for-byte instead (see `recaptureNote`).

partialCapture.recaptureNote: Re-captured in place, at the rebased head, and the result is one-sided: 101 of the 108 frames came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and all 48 of the four Files surfaces plus all 12 control frames are among them. The 7 that moved are media-viewer frames - pdf 1 (`localOperatorDark`), image 2 (`synth`, `radient`), audio 2 (`neon`, `radient`), video 2 (`synth`, `radient`) - and six of the seven moved only at the lossy encoder's own quantisation scale: at an 8% tolerance (20/255) ZERO pixels differ, and the worst RMSE is 0.00054 (`video-viewer/radient`, 4,342 px of 1,152,000). That class is established rather than assumed: the same command on the same tree was run twice in the previous pass, and `audio-viewer/neon` - which moved in both passes' first runs - came back EXACTLY the committed bytes in one of them, so the movement is the widget repaint and the encoder and a frame that has moved is not read as a change unless it survives a second run. The seventh, `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, is a reproducible platform paint failure and not that class: this session's private headless Chrome never painted the PDF guest document - a probe at 640,200 reads the platform field `srgb(40,40,40)` where the committed frame reads the white page - with a byte-for-byte identical difference (204,364 px, 163,673 of them above 8%) in both passes. The viewer's own source (`pdf-preview.tsx`, `canvas-file-viewer.tsx`, the story) is untouched by `main`'s move, and this branch's canvas hunks in `chat-page.tsx` and `chat-content.tsx` - the one host surface the rebase had to carry - survive line-for-line, so the committed frame is the one that depicts the surface under review; it is retained and NO byte-identity claim is made for it. The 7 frames whose committed bytes are retained are the same picture the re-capture measured.
partialCapture.addedAtHeadNote: This is the pass that ADDED the twelve `canvas-workspace--files-scan-stopped-empty` frames, cited as the replay of the head it ran on: the original `58d3dfc05` is no longer reachable from any ref after an earlier force-push, its replay `46684b07e` was orphaned by the rebase onto 0.19.6, that replay's replay `5d2a04778` was orphaned by the rebase onto `fb9c0942e`, and its next replay `9bf8a6357` was orphaned in turn by this rebase onto `98c32e85e` - so the citation is this rebase's replay, `a32475ed5`. These pairs are not range-diff `=` where they differ at all: their patches differ in this rebase's spelling of the manifest alone, because that file's prose and counters were re-based on the new `main` on both sides, so every frame and every source path that commit carries is the same one, which is the property a citation is for. That run is also the first whose cache lives inside the scratch root: `run.sh` now sets `HOME="$SCRATCH/home"` (QA round 2, Q3 — the catalogue cache resolves from `HOME`, not from the config dir), so the seed copies the same `*.listing.json` files the earlier run read into the scratch home, and nothing outside `/tmp` is written. supplementary.why: the claim is that a hover, a keyboard highlight, an in-flight pick and the OUTCOME of that pick are perceivable — properties of computed style and of timing that no palette assertion and no component test can see. The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). Seven of the sixteen states are after-only, and that is the finding rather than an omission: each is a state the old code could not produce or could not report — the pointer's structural edge in a palette where the wash collapses (D12), the footer naming the row Enter acts on while that row is off screen (U1), the band holding a labelled spinner while the pick is unconfirmed (U3), the refusal landing with the dialog already closed (U2), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames (Q1). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.
